To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the majority of early-stage prostate patients are not aware of the potential side-effects of treatment, and that they would like information about the side-effects of treatment.
the information needs of early-stage PCa patients are similar across countries.
the information needs of early-stage patients with prostate cancer (PC) differ between the countries studied.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the information needs of early-stage PCa patients and their carers.
the information needs of early-stage (T1-T2) prostate cancer patients.
the development of a model for the analysis of information needs of early-stage patients with prostate cancer in different countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is a paucity of information on the information needs of patients with prostate cancer, especially at the early stages of the disease, and that there is an urgent need to conduct more research to address this issue.
the information needs of men with prostate cancer differ between countries.
there is no evidence to support or contradict that the use of a specific dietary pattern, or a specific dietary component, is effective in the primary and secondary prevention of prostate cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found a large variation in the information needs of patients with prostate cancer.

the information needs of early-stage PCa patients vary considerably among the countries and are influenced by the national health care system, cultural and religious beliefs, and the level of education of the patient.
the information needs of patients with early-stage prostate cancer vary across different countries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the majority of patients are satisfied with the information they receive, although there is a subset of men who are not satisfied and would prefer more information.
the information needs of men with prostate cancer are similar across countries and that these needs are not being met.
the current system of prostate-specific antigen (PSA)-based screening is not working, and we should move toward a more targeted approach.
